title: AI and the future of electronic medical records
text:
The EMR (electronic medical record) has been the bane of front-line physicians for 2 decades, documenting clinical details (most often hand typing) to meet billing levels so you are adequately reimbursed.  In addition, dealing with insurers to appeal denials, etc.  All of this is not really "doctoring" but the system mandates it. Revolutionizing the current workflow in most patient encounters will be the primary goal where AI is helping. Forms of "ambient AI" that is in the background that collects the patient interaction and pulls in background info from the EMR are beginning to take hold. This is not high-level decision making but simply eliminating drudgery.  For complex scenarios (with large patient charts over years), having AI scrub for key data to facilitate an encounter increases efficiency.  These "low hanging fruit" to reduce admin burden is where the current emphasis needs to be (before humanoid robots, etc.).  The major tension is that majority of EMR (and patient records) is concentrated in a single private family-owned company (Epic). That will become an issue for deploying innovative AI tools.

Hoping for the AI bots to rapidly transform documentation and other admin functions in healthcare.  That should not cost many jobs per se, but increase needed efficiency to allow empathy back in?
